name: Ruby
title: Ruby (4.0)

presenceList.meta: R1, G3, Q2, Q3, Ec6, Ec7

preamble.text: Analysis against Ruby 4.0 (December 2025). YJIT is production-ready since Ruby 3.2+.

type.text: **Duck typing**: No compile-time type checking, coupling invisible
**Pattern matching (3.0+) is not exhaustive**: A `case`/`in` with no `else` raises `NoMatchingPatternError` at run time rather than reporting a missing case
**Mixins**: Include modules for behavior without inheritance
**Open classes**: Can modify any class, creates action-at-a-distance coupling
**RBS type signatures**: External type system (`.rbs` files) — static checking via Steep/Sorbet, not built into runtime
**Method_missing**: Dynamic dispatch hides coupling, runtime failures

construction.text: **Data.define (3.2+)**: Immutable value objects like records/kotlin data classes
**Class methods for factories**: Common pattern but not enforced
**No validation enforcement**: Constructor invariants not checked
**Monkey patching**: Can modify any class anywhere, global coupling
**Class variables**: `@@var` shared across all instances, couples classes

memory.text: **GC pauses**: Non-deterministic, couples performance to runtime (improved by YJIT's reduced allocation rate)
**YJIT reduces GC pressure**: Faster execution means fewer long-lived allocations

error.text: **Pattern matching with `=>` operator (3.0+)**: Can destructure error objects structurally
**Silent failures**: Methods often return nil instead of raising

concurrency.text: **Global VM Lock (GVL)**: Like Python's GIL, couples threads to single core
**Fibers + Fiber Scheduler (3.0+)**: Cooperative concurrency with io_uring support for async I/O
**M:N thread scheduler (3.3+, experimental → progressing)**: Lightweight userspace threads
**Shared mutable state**: No protection, race conditions easy

platform.text: **No company owns the language**: Ruby is developed by the ruby-core community under the Ruby Licence, dual-licensed with the two-clause BSD licence
**Several implementations exist**: MRI (Matz's Ruby Interpreter) is the reference implementation, alongside JRuby on the JVM, TruffleRuby on GraalVM, and mruby for embedded use
**The runtime is portable**: MRI builds on Linux, macOS, Windows through RubyInstaller, and the BSDs
**The JVM is an available target**: JRuby runs the same language on the Java platform, so Ruby code is not confined to one runtime
**Packaging is vendor-neutral**: RubyGems and Bundler fetch gems from any repository, not from one vendor's service

performance.text: **YJIT (production-ready since 3.2)**: 3-5x speedup in many benchmarks; reduced GC pressure
**GVL**: Couples multithreading to single core (still present in Ruby 4.0)
**The JIT is opt-in**: YJIT must be enabled with `--yjit` or `RUBY_YJIT_ENABLE=1`, so a default run stays interpreted
**High memory**: Object overhead significant (partially offset by YJIT)
**Optimization hard**: Dynamic nature limits static optimization

ecosystem.text: **Rails dominates the ecosystem**: Most Ruby applications are Rails applications, so the framework's conventions and release cycle set the pace for the rest

evolution.text: **RBS/Sorbet**: Type signatures external, not core language

domain.text: **Excellent for web**: Rails is industry standard
**Good for scripting**: Clean syntax for automation
**Improved for performance-sensitive**: YJIT closes gap but still slower than compiled languages

learning.text: **Excellent resources**: Why's Poignant Guide, Rails tutorials

testing.text: **Test culture**: TDD/BDD strong in Ruby community

security.text: **Rails security**: Framework helps, but language-level gaps

tradeoffs: **Programmer happiness is the design goal**: Ruby favours expressive code over enforcement, a deliberate trade of static guarantees for code that reads like prose
**Parentheses are optional**: The grammar treats a method call and a local variable alike, a readability choice whose cost is ambiguity in dense expressions
**Everything is an object**: Numbers, strings, and classes all respond to methods, a uniform model that removes special-case rules and adds method lookup to every value
**Visibility is cooperative**: `private` and `protected` can be bypassed with `send`, so encapsulation is a convention the language does not enforce — a deliberate openness rather than a dependency
verdict: Ruby prioritizes developer happiness over low coupling by language design. Pattern matching (3.0+) and Data.define (3.2+) add structured data handling. YJIT transforms performance. Main strength: readable, expressive syntax makes intent clear. Main weakness: all coupling detection deferred to runtime, metaprogramming creates invisible dependencies, GVL persists.

energy.text: Interpreted by default: the slowest class in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: A large training corpus and strong code-generation results: models write this language well [@joel2025lowresource; @effibenchx2025].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.
